text:
maria: Pushed silica9b-v2 (int4 per-channel) to canary overnight. Bench OK but we're getting intermittent OOMs in production-like traffic.

sam: Can you share the canary route config and a sample OOM log? Any correlation with long prompts / max_new_tokens?

maria: route config pasted:
model: silica9b-v2; batching: batch_size=8, batch_window_ms=12; defaults: max_new_tokens=512, prefetch=true, soft_reserve=0.3
OOM excerpt: AllocFailed cudaMalloc trying 1.2GiB; slab_free_list low-water, fragmentation=0.48; last-op=kv_prefetch + continuous_batch commit

li: Two quick hypotheses: (1) large max_new_tokens + prefetch builds big KV caches, fragmenting the slab under microbursts; (2) batch window + slowgen causes long-lived buffers.

noah: Short-term mitigation proposed: set defaults.max_new_tokens=128, batching.batch_window_ms=6, defaults.prefetch=false, defaults.soft_reserve=0.2, enable kv_eviction_threshold=0.75.

maria: Command to patch canary: redwoodctl models update --model silica9b-v2 --env canary --set "defaults.max_new_tokens=128" --set "defaults.prefetch=false" --set "batching.batch_window_ms=6" --set "defaults.soft_reserve=0.2"

sam: I'll also push infra patch: lower slab freelist high-water and enable slot_compactor on canary nodes. Deploying now.

li: Longer term: run quant-sensitivity eval (int4 per-channel vs int8 hybrid) and a max_new_tokens/batch_size sweep [64,128,256] x [2,4,8], dataset 2k short+long prompts. Measure 99/99.9 latency, OOM rate, and token-efficiency.

maria: Kicking off eval after we stabilize canary. Lowering traffic to 5% until validated. Will collect auto-batching profiles too.

sam: If OOMs persist, we can emergency-fallback nodes to int8 kernel per-node. Ping me to trigger.

deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/infra/slot-compactor-v0.3 -> canary (3 nodes). Status updates to follow.

maria: Applied defaults patch; monitoring 10m window. Will report back. :rocket:
